findings.text: Intrusive doubly linked insertion centers on a core helper that links a fresh element between a stated predecessor and successor after consulting a validity helper and skipping the update on rejection. Public wrappers place the element directly after a head, directly before a head to achieve tail insertion, or at the tail with release ordering for the final publication step.

Removal centers on a core helper that joins the predecessor and successor of a condemned element. Entry helpers validate before unlinking and then either leave one residual link cleared to null, overwrite both residual links with poison markers, reinitialise the element as an empty self linked list, or reinitialise with ordered publication for concurrent observers.

Rearrangement reuses unlink plus link primitives. One operation exchanges an old element for a new element at the same position, optionally reinitialising the old element. Another exchanges the positions of two elements. Further operations relocate an element to the front or back of a list, relocate a contiguous run delimited by first and last markers to the tail of another list, move the first element to the tail when nonempty, or rotate a chosen element to the front by relocating a head marker.

List shape is tested without mutation. Empty means the head forward link refers to the head itself, observed with a single load. Singular means nonempty with identical forward and backward links. Additional tests report whether an element is the first after a head, the last before a head, or identical with the head. A careful empty test combines an acquire load of the forward link with a plain load of the backward link and carries an explicit annotation recording intentional lockless access.

Insertion and removal validation has two build shapes. One shape always accepts. The other shape for removal first checks mutual consistency between the element and its neighbours by confirming each neighbour points back, accepting immediately on success and otherwise combining a failure flag with the outcome of a further reporting check. Callers skip mutation when validation reports failure.

Lists can be divided and joined. Cutting transfers an initial segment up to and including a chosen entry, or up to but excluding a chosen entry, into a separate head. Empty input leaves the destination untouched or reinitialised depending on the variant, a head position reinitialises the destination, and a stated singular corner is ignored. Splicing inserts an entire source list after a head or before a head, optionally reinitialising the source, and does nothing when the source is empty.

Conversion between links and enclosing records is by member offset. Helpers fetch the record owning the first link, the last link, the successor link or the predecessor link, with circular variants that wrap to the opposite end at the boundary. Null returning forms yield null when the examined forward or backward link equals the head, using single or acquire loads. A preparation helper replaces a null cursor with the record derived from the head, and a head membership test compares a record member address with a head.

Traversal is offered as iteration macros over raw links and over enclosing records. Raw forms walk forward, backward, from a successor onward, or with a prefetched successor that tolerates removal of the current link. Record forms walk forward or reverse from either end, continue after the current record, resume from the current record, or use prefetched neighbours for safe removal, with a helper to refresh the cached successor after manual cursor changes. A tally helper counts nodes by walking forward.

Single headed hash lists are observed to use a head with a field named first holding either null or a node address, and nodes with a field named next holding either null or a successor plus a field named pprev holding the address of the preceding forward link. Empty is denoted by null first. A special fake state points pprev at the node own next field, and singularity for a node relative to a head means no successor with pprev aimed at the head first field.

Hash list mutation inserts a node at the head or immediately before or behind a stated node, removes a node while poisoning residual links, transfers a whole chain between two heads leaving the source empty, or prepends one chain before another while emptying the source. Lookup and traversal convert nodes to enclosing records with null safe helpers and walk raw nodes or records forward, including safe forms that prefetch the successor. A tally helper counts nodes and a lockless test reports unhashed when the preceding link is null.

Bit locked hash lists declare a head type with a single pointer field named first and a node type with pointer fields named next and pprev. The low bit of the head first pointer carries a lock while the remaining bits carry the true first node address or null. Initialisers set the head first to null and node links to null. Dedicated accessors mask out the lock bit to read the true first node, check alignment and locked state when installing a new first node, and test emptiness by masking a single load of first.

Bit locked mutation inserts at the head or before or behind a stated node while preserving any lock bit held in an affected head link, unlinks through a helper that merges the successor with the preserved lock bit, poisons residual links on plain removal, or conditionally unlinks and reinitialises only when currently hashed. Unhashed means a null preceding link. Record conversion is by member offset and traversal walks from the masked first node forward, with a safe form that prefetches the successor.

Ordinary doubly linked updates publish exactly one forward link with an ordered single store or release store while companion links use plain stores, and observers use single or acquire loads for emptiness and first element checks. Careful deletion separates plain reinitialisation of one link from release publication of the other. Hash insertions use ordered single stores throughout. Bit locked heads use a bit spin lock on bit zero with acquire and release annotations plus a locked query, and lock bit preserving stores are used when the updated preceding link may be the head first field.

A doubly linked element moves among empty self linked, linked with mutually consistent neighbours, and removed with poisoned or reinitialised links. A hash node moves among unhashed with null preceding link, hashed with a valid preceding link, fake with a self referential preceding link, and removed with poisoned links. A bit locked node moves between unhashed null and hashed valid, while its head moves between unlocked and locked distinguished solely by the low lock bit independent of list membership.

Most helpers assume external exclusion except the explicitly careful and lockless forms, so concurrent mutation without holding the appropriate lock can corrupt links. One build configuration disables validation entirely and propagates corrupt links. Bulk move, cut, splice, replace, swap and singular checks dereference caller supplied positions with only the stated degenerate guards. Poisoned links must never be dereferenced and fake hash nodes must never be mistaken for hashed membership. Installing a new bit locked first pointer assumes the head is already locked.

The bit locked mask has two build variants, one denoting an unsigned long value of one and one denoting an unsigned long value of zero. A bug check helper either forwards its condition to a trap or expands to no operation depending on build. Two header guard identifiers protect the bit locked and nulls headers, and the hash head empty initializer denotes null first with static and automatic declaration forms.

The durable entry surface for circular lists is insertion after or before a head, removal with optional reinitialisation, relocation to front or back, splicing whole lists after or before a head with optional source reinitialisation, cutting segments into a new head, plus shape tests, record accessors, traversals and tallies. Hash lists add head, before and behind insertion with removal, chain move and splice. Bit locked lists add the same mutation shape plus explicit lock, unlock and locked query operations.
